scope.workflowBoundary: The qualified slice is the Sales-owned price-list lifecycle that the Quotes catalogue flow requires before a quotation is prepared: create a dated Company/customer draft, edit that draft under an expected version, then activate it by an independent Company sales manager or cancel it. It is not the quotation/sales-order document itself. Quote/order draft create/update remains Commerce-owned; quote/order transitions, fulfillment, cancellation, revenue handoff and customer notifications remain retained.
scope.domain: Current Sales actor policy (sales module, selected-context expiry, commerce.read + commerce.sales, commerce.approve for decisions, Company scope only), bounded name/currency/customer/date/discount/item facts, exact two-decimal minor-unit prices, one line per product, 1..500 lines, draft-only edit/decision matrix, expected-version CAS, independent activation against both creator and latest preparer, and exact receipt `{id,status,version}` plus persisted readback validation.
scope.application: Every command serializes its idempotency key, resolves the exact prior receipt before a fresh write, rechecks current IAM, verifies the Company currency and active customer/product sources before the write, applies one expected-version write, rechecks currency/customer/product sources after the write, validates the persisted list and item rows, then inserts the shared receipt, audit and outbox records in the same caller-owned serializable Holding transaction. No transaction is opened, committed or retried here.
scope.adapters: SQL ownership is explicit. `sales_price_lists` and `sales_price_list_items` are Sales-owned and the only business rows mutated. `commerce_settings`, `finance_parties` and `commerce_products` are read-only same-transaction source facts used by the retained owner flow. `command_receipts`, `audit_events` and `outbox_events` are shared Workflow records. No Commerce, Finance or Inventory mutation SQL is introduced.
scope.http: Owner-local POST /api/v1/holdings/{holding_slug}/sales/pricing, /sales/pricing/{price_list_id}/edit and /sales/pricing/{price_list_id}. Exact registered Host/Holding targets, exact HTTPS Origin when supplied, Idempotency-Key (8..100 chars), application/json, bounded 256 KiB body, strict exact JSON keys, decimal-price parsing to minor units, bounded business-error mapping, private/no-store, no-referrer and nosniff responses. The composition backend receives transport facts only and must supply the normal Account session, current Company scope, feature/module admission and serializable owner unit.
scope.transport: ERPX_NATIVE_SALES_PRICING_CONFIG is strictly validated by the client: loopback-only private base, reserved ports 3000/3001/3100/3101/3103/8080 plus 5432/5433/5435 and 3200-3299 excluded, exact HTTPS Holding origins, unique hosts/slugs, 250..30000 ms timeout, bounded cookie/context headers, exact receipt shape, context CAS coherence and a 64 KiB response bound. A configured failure never falls back to the retained TypeScript command.
scope.routeCutover: The retained Commerce pricing POST branch selects the native command when the selector is configured and otherwise keeps savePriceList/updatePriceList/decidePriceList. The existing production module admission remains in front of the branch; once the native command is selected, a configured failure is surfaced rather than replaced.
